0.reason: layout: the comparison panels render narrower than their columns, but labels are legible, nothing overlaps, and the detail panel carries the X-point comparison the record cites

findings.summary: The three panels are given equal-width columns while each poloidal panel keeps an equal aspect ratio, so the two panels that carry the comparison the figure exists for render at roughly 40 percent of their allotted width and the detail panel dominates the canvas. In both attached renders the machine cross-section spans about 250 px of a 1714 px canvas, while the right-hand zoom fills nearly its whole third; between the first and second panel there is a blank band wider than either poloidal drawing. The consequence for a reader is that the two full-geometry panels -- the side-by-side comparison of the original against the best rigid translation, with both contour families and both null pairs on each -- are drawn at the smallest scale on the page, and the 32.6 cm and 26.2 cm axis offsets they exist to show are read across a smaller distance than the detail panel's own zoom, which shows only the lower null. Nothing becomes unreadable, which is why this does not hold the node: both families, both axes and both lower nulls are distinguishable in every panel. A width ratio favouring the two geometry panels, or drawing the two geometry panels as equal-height columns with the zoom sized to the same scale, would remove the wasted band and enlarge the comparison without changing any data.

item_verdicts.nova_rules: Axis off on every poloidal panel: met. Wall drawn in every panel: met (a full limiter polyline in the two geometry panels, the local wall segments in the zoom). Solved and reference nulls both drawn, with distinct shapes and the reference drawn later at a higher layer: met, and visible as such. Scalar maps as line contours on shared levels: met -- both families sit on the one physical level array the in-image text names. Labels in the margin: met.
item_verdicts.numbers_against_the_receipt: The values printed inside each image reconcile with the reviewed run's own stored receipt: 137 lower-X offset (0.82125, 7.24945) cm gives 7.30 cm before and 9.90 cm after; 146 (2.78155, 5.97315) cm gives 6.59 cm before and 7.44 cm after; the fitted translations are (+0.08410, -0.00887) m and (+0.09217, -0.02241) m, matching the printed (+8.41, -0.89) cm and (+9.22, -2.24) cm. Frame 137's printed numbers match the frame-137 render exactly; frame 146's match its own. So the text a reader sees on the picture is the receipt's, not a stale transcription.
